loops.loop: Why would God command His conquering army to march around the strongest walls in the world in total silence -- no war cries, no noise -- instead of attacking?
loops.note: No line ever states WHY silence was commanded -- the word 'silence' itself never returns. The loop pays off only by dramatic contrast: six days of enforced quiet erupt, on the seventh, into 'a great shout' that brings the wall down in the very next clause. That is a real show-not-tell payoff (matches Joshua 6:10, where the silence is broken exactly at the commanded shout) but it is closed by implication, not by an explicit callback to 'silence.' Creator call: accept as-is -- adding one clause like 'the silence finally broke' would make it explicit if a future re-cut wants it.

loops.loop: Why one scarlet cord, specifically, hanging from one window -- singled out as the very last image before the hook ends on Rahab?
loops.payoff_phrase: scarlet line running from her window to a cross

loops.loop: Who is Rahab -- introduced only as 'a woman with a past' -- and why does she matter enough to be named inside a city about to be destroyed?
loops.payoff_phrase: By faith the harlot Rahab perished not

loops.loop: Does Rahab's 'past' ever connect to anything larger, or is she left behind once the walls fall?
loops.payoff_phrase: The woman behind the scarlet cord became His family
